newsitem.title: USA: U.S. insurers group backs choice on airbags - paper.
newsitem.headline: U.S. insurers group backs choice on airbags - paper.

text.p: Changing position, the Insurance Institute for Highway Safety has recommended the federal government allow consumers to deactivate air bags in their cars, the Washington Post reported Wednesday.
The Institute played a key role in persuading the government to require air bags in cars and has been an advocate of the protective devices for three decades.

But the institute said if the government does not allow deactivation, public pressure might lead to elimination of the requirement that cars be equipped with air bags. The Institute, headquartered in Virginia, sent its views to the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration in February, the Post said.
The NHTSA, which requires car owners to get its permission before disconnecting air bags, is considering a proposal that anyone be allowed to decide whether to deactivate the bags.
Consumer advocates criticized the Institute's new policy. Automakers also said they opposed the group's new position.
"This is a pretty tough call," said Institute president Brian O'Neill.
"It's hard to characterize our position, except to say that it reflects the realities as they are today. It's a strategic concession," he told the Post.
